requirements.statement: A Viewer of a project can include it in a bundle and receives its code in the download, but cannot rename the plugin or change the source system through the bundle path; a project with no role for the caller is absent from the selection and a guessed id returns 403 with no code.

requirements.source_phrase: Version Labels: Let you name important saved versions
requirements.statement: A Viewer can read version labels and notes but a PATCH naming, renaming or clearing a label is refused with no stored change, while the same request from an Editor succeeds; a Viewer's restore request is likewise refused.

requirements.source_phrase: Project Zip Export: Package the .h, .cpp and setup guide with its Why notes into one download ready to drop into a UE5 project
requirements.statement: If a project's stored C++ or setup content is missing or the zip build throws, the export action shows an error naming the missing part and downloads no partial zip, leaving the project unchanged.

A view-only /share/{token} page offers the UE5 .zip plugin export for the shared project and downloads the same plugin folder as the owner's export, without exposing project files or any editing control.
requirements.notes: Build description: share-link pages have their own UE5 .zip button and offer the plugin; inherited R-070 and R-071 keep the share view read-only and file-free.

requirements.source_phrase: Built-in check plus AI review
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/review-cpp reads the key, provider and model only from the X-LLM-* headers, calls the selected provider once per review, returns a provider refusal or timeout as a plain error, and writes the key into no log line, response or stored record, including in provider URLs logged on error.
requirements.notes: Third-party and secret hygiene: inherited R-167 covers leak checks; this covers the new review path.

requirements.source_phrase: Instant built-in check; Built-in check plus AI review
requirements.statement: The built-in compile check on a generated system completes without a network call and within about a second when the C++ tab is opened, and switching back to the C++ tab does not start a provider review.

requirements.source_phrase: Plugin Export: Offer the zip as a ready-made Unreal plugin, with its own module files, so it installs with no code edits
requirements.statement: The UE5 .zip export menu is reachable from the workspace top bar and from a public share page in the deployed app, and both entries download a zip built from the project data already loaded with no server-side zip service.

requirements.source_phrase: That line is highlighted and the code viewers show line numbers.
requirements.statement: The .h and .cpp code viewers show a line-number column whose numbers match the actual line positions and do not drift when the code scrolls or a jump highlights a line.
requirements.notes: Build features: line-number gutter present in CodeBox.jsx.

requirements.source_phrase: clicking an issue in the compile check (or in the export warning) opens the C++ tab and scrolls to the matching file and line.
requirements.statement: Clicking an issue row in the export-check warning modal closes the modal, opens the C++ tab, and performs the same file-and-line jump as the compile-check row, without starting an export.
requirements.notes: Build features: export-check-issues rows clickable -> closes modal, jumps to line. The export stays available and is not triggered by the click.

requirements.source_phrase: one button sends the current issues (built-in and AI review) with both files to your own AI key.
requirements.statement: The compile-check header's Fix these button sends the current built-in and AI-review issues together with the .h and .cpp files to the saved AI key, shows a running state, and opens the before/after review without changing code until Accept is pressed.
requirements.notes: Build features: compile-check-panel, fix-all-button, fix-modal, fix-running.

requirements.source_phrase: The AI returns only the lines that need changing, and the rest of the code stays as it is.
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp with file_base, cpp_header, cpp_source and the current issues returns 200 with cpp_header and cpp_source containing only the changed lines while every unrelated line remains byte-identical, plus a changes list and the model used; with no X-LLM-Key it returns 400 and stores nothing.
requirements.notes: Build API: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp {file_base,cpp_header,cpp_source,issues[]} -> {cpp_header,cpp_source,changes,model} or 422; 400 without key. Patch-only means the response is the edited source, not a regenerated system.

requirements.source_phrase: each issue row also has a small "Fix" action that patches just that one problem, through the same before/after review.
requirements.statement: Each issue row has a Fix action that sends only that issue to the fix endpoint, opens the same before/after review, and produces a patch that addresses that issue while leaving unrelated code unchanged.
requirements.notes: Build features: compile-issues-fix-N per row.

requirements.source_phrase: With no key saved, the key window opens.
requirements.statement: With no saved AI key, pressing Fix these or a row's Fix opens the AI key window and sends no fix request; after a key is saved the same action runs the fix with that key.
requirements.notes: The key window is the same AI key modal inherited from R-146/R-150.

requirements.source_phrase: Fixes use the user's own AI key and current model, never the Universal Key.
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp with no user key or with an 'sk-emergent' key returns 400 naming the missing user key and makes no provider call; no server-side Universal Key is used as a fallback for any fix request.
requirements.notes: The fallback is the thing to disprove: a patch returned with no user key means the owner key is still wired in.

requirements.source_phrase: the proposed fix opens in a side-by-side diff of the .h and .cpp with changed lines marked.
requirements.statement: The fix review modal shows side-by-side .h and .cpp diffs with removed lines in red and added lines in green, a short change list explaining each change, and Accept fix and Discard buttons; Accept replaces the workspace code as an unsaved edit and Discard closes the modal with the original code unchanged.
requirements.notes: Build features: fix-change-list, fix-diff-h, fix-diff-cpp, fix-accept, fix-discard. Nothing changes without approval.

requirements.source_phrase: A progress state shows while the AI works.
requirements.statement: Pressing Fix these or a row's Fix opens the fix modal immediately with a visible running state and disabled Accept/Discard, then replaces the running state with the diff or an error; closing the modal before completion leaves the code unchanged.
requirements.notes: Build features: fix-running inside fix-modal.

requirements.source_phrase: If the AI returns a patch that can't be applied cleanly (lines no longer match), the review shows an error and offers to try again. Nothing changes.
requirements.statement: When the fix endpoint returns patch_failed or no_changes, the fix modal shows a plain-English error naming the cause and a Retry button, and the workspace code is unchanged; pressing Retry calls the endpoint again with the same issues and files.
requirements.notes: Build features: fix-error + fix-retry.

requirements.source_phrase: If the AI returns a patch that can't be applied cleanly (lines no longer match), the review shows an error and offers to try again. Nothing changes.
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp returns 422 with detail.code 'patch_failed' or 'no_changes' and a message when the model's patch cannot be applied or contains no changes, writes no code to the project, and a later retry with the same input makes a new provider call rather than replaying the cached failure.
requirements.notes: Build API: 422 {detail:{code:'patch_failed'|'no_changes',message}}.

requirements.source_phrase: on accept, the compile check runs again automatically. It shows a result such as "Cleared 4 of 5 issues", and any remaining or new issues stay listed.
requirements.statement: After Accept fix, the compile check reruns automatically on the updated workspace code, shows a result of the form 'Cleared X of Y issues' where X equals the issues no longer found and Y equals the issues before the fix, and lists any remaining or newly found issues for further fix, ignore or copy.
requirements.notes: Build features: automatic re-check and 'Cleared X of Y' toast; the check itself runs client-side over the stored/edited code.

requirements.source_phrase: An accepted fix changes only the workspace code. It isn't saved until the user presses Save, and it can be undone by discarding changes or from version history.
requirements.statement: After Accept fix the workspace shows the patched .h and .cpp but a page reload before Save shows the last saved code; a Discard changes action restores the last saved code without creating a version, and restoring a version from history also replaces the unsaved fix.
requirements.notes: Accept is a local workspace edit; Save is the only persistence path, and version restore is inherited from R-176/R-177.

requirements.source_phrase: Accepting a fix doesn't count as a "change for next synthesis". It replaces the current code directly, so the regenerate button doesn't light up for it.
requirements.statement: After Accept fix the 'Queued for next synthesis' list has no new entry and the Regenerate button's change count is unchanged, while the patched code is what the next Save stores and what the next synthesis sends as current code.
requirements.notes: Check the queued list and the button count, not only that the code changed.

requirements.source_phrase: This costs 1 request and counts toward the daily usage counter.
requirements.statement: Each Fix these or single-issue fix request that reaches the provider increments the signed-in user's daily usage count by one per attempt actually sent, including a retry, and the usage chip reflects the new count when the fix modal closes.
requirements.notes: Extends inherited R-174/R-175 to the fix path; a retried provider call counts once per attempt.

requirements.source_phrase: Before running, Fix these warns when the daily free limit is near, the same way synthesis does now.
requirements.statement: When the selected model's daily usage is near its free limit, pressing Fix these shows a warning naming the used count and offering Cancel, run the fix anyway, or switch to the free Gemini model with the most quota left; no request reaches the provider until a choice is made.
requirements.notes: Same choices as the inherited synthesis limit warning R-182.

requirements.source_phrase: Before running, Fix these warns when the daily free limit is near, the same way synthesis does now.
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp checks the caller's daily usage before any provider call and, when the selected model is at or above the configured warning threshold, returns a limit_warning response carrying used and limit with no provider request; the same request with confirm_limit=true makes exactly one provider call and one usage increment.
requirements.notes: Mirrors R-183 for the fix endpoint; nothing is sent before the confirmation.

requirements.source_phrase: any built-in warning or error can be marked "Ignore". It's hidden from the count, the tab badge and the export warning, and listed under a collapsible "Ignored (N)" section where it can be restored.
requirements.statement: Each built-in compile-check issue row has an Ignore action; pressing it hides that issue from the issue list, count, C++ tab badge and export warning, adds it to a collapsible 'Ignored (N)' section with its file, line and message, and a Restore action in that section puts it back into the active list.
requirements.notes: Build features: compile-issues-ignore-N, ignored-toggle, ignored-issues, ignored-issues-restore-N.

requirements.source_phrase: Ignores are saved with the project, so teammates see them too.
requirements.statement: PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores stores the ignored built-in issue keys for the project, GET /api/projects/{id} returns them as ignored_issues, and a second identical PUT is idempotent; the ignored keys are scoped to that project and returned to every member with read access.
requirements.notes: Build API: PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores; GET project returns ignored_issues.

requirements.source_phrase: It's hidden from the count, the tab badge and the export warning, and listed under a collapsible "Ignored (N)" section where it can be restored.
requirements.statement: The C++ tab badge, the compile-check summary and the export warning count only non-ignored issues; when every issue is ignored the badge is absent, the summary reads no likely mistakes, and the export warning is skipped, while the 'Ignored (N)' count equals the number of stored ignores.
requirements.notes: Build features: cpp-issue-badge and compile-check-summary exclude ignored; ignored-toggle shows count.

requirements.source_phrase: Ignores are saved with the project, so teammates see them too.
requirements.statement: After ignoring an issue and reloading or reopening the project in a new session, the issue is still under 'Ignored (N)' and still excluded from the count; a teammate with read access opening the same project sees the same ignored set.
requirements.notes: Persistence and the second actor; a browser-only ignore fails the teammate half.

requirements.source_phrase: An ignore stops applying if that issue's line text changes.
requirements.statement: An ignore is applied only while the stored line text for that issue is unchanged; when the issue's line text differs on the next check, GET /api/projects/{id}/ignores no longer suppresses it and the issue appears in the active list again.
requirements.notes: The ignore key must carry enough line identity to compare old and new text; a file+line-only key would wrongly suppress a new issue at the same line.

requirements.source_phrase: Ignores apply to built-in check issues only in phase 1. AI review findings are refreshed each run.
requirements.statement: Ignores apply only to built-in check issues in this phase: an AI-review finding has no ignore key, cannot be added to PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores, and is recomputed on each AI review rather than suppressed by the project's ignored_issues list.
requirements.notes: Phase 2 says ignoring AI-review findings is deferred; Phase 1 must reject it.

requirements.source_phrase: a "Copy issues" button puts a plain-text list on the clipboard: file, line, message and suggested fix. Ignored items are excluded.
requirements.statement: The compile-check header's Copy issues button puts a plain-text list on the clipboard with one entry per non-ignored issue naming its file, line, message and suggested fix, shows a confirmation, and excludes every issue listed under 'Ignored (N)'.
requirements.notes: Build features: copy-issues-button; the clipboard content is judged by pasting it, not by the button's disabled state.

requirements.statement: With no non-ignored issues, Copy issues copies an empty list or shows a 'No issues to copy' message and does not throw or copy stale clipboard content.
requirements.notes: Tier-1 empty state of the copy action; a clean system still has the button.

requirements.source_phrase: from the bundle window, "Save as preset" stores the plugin name and chosen projects under a name such as "Survival Kit".
requirements.statement: The bundle dialog has a Save as preset action that prompts for a name and stores the current plugin name and selected project ids as a preset, and the preset then appears in a 'Bundle presets' list in the Projects panel.
requirements.notes: Build features: bundle-plugin-button, bundle-save-preset (window.prompt), bundle-presets list.

requirements.source_phrase: Team presets follow the existing rule: visible to anyone who can open all of their projects.
requirements.statement: POST /api/bundle-presets stores a preset with its name, plugin_name, project ids and optional team, owned by the caller; GET /api/bundle-presets returns the caller's own presets plus presets shared with them through a team or project access for which the caller can open every project, each carrying its creator's name; PATCH renames and DELETE removes a preset only for its creator, and an invalid plugin_name returns 422 and stores nothing.
requirements.notes: Amended: the user enabled sharing of presets among teammates, so the list is no longer owner-only; rename and delete stay creator-only.

requirements.source_phrase: A "Bundle presets" list in the Projects panel re-opens a preset with its projects already ticked, using their latest saved versions.
requirements.statement: Opening a preset from the Projects panel opens the bundle dialog with the preset's plugin name and its saved projects ticked from their latest saved versions, and lists any missing or no-longer-accessible projects as skipped without failing the open.
requirements.notes: Build features: preset-open-{id}; missing id shows bundle-skipped.

requirements.source_phrase: Missing or no-longer-accessible projects are listed as skipped.
requirements.statement: When a preset's project list contains an id that is missing or no longer readable by the caller, GET /api/bundle-presets/{id} returns the readable project ids and a skipped list naming the missing ids, and a bundle built from it contains modules only for the readable projects.
requirements.notes: Build features: bundle-skipped; a missing project must not fail the whole preset or produce an empty module.

requirements.source_phrase: Presets can be renamed and deleted.
requirements.statement: Each row in the Bundle presets list has rename and delete controls; rename updates the preset's displayed name in place, delete removes the row after confirmation, and both changes persist after a page reload.
requirements.notes: Build features: preset-rename-{id}, preset-delete-{id}.

requirements.source_phrase: Anyone who can open all its projects
requirements.statement: A preset is returned to a non-creator only while that user can open every project in it and is omitted as soon as one of its projects is unreadable for them, and PATCH or DELETE by anyone other than its creator returns 403 with no stored change.
requirements.notes: Amended: the earlier owner-only isolation is reversed for visibility by the user's instruction, while the creator-only mutation boundary is kept.

requirements.source_phrase: using their latest saved versions.
requirements.statement: Opening a preset and downloading its bundle reads each selected project's current saved system at download time, so a project saved after the preset was created contributes its latest version rather than the version captured when the preset was saved.
requirements.notes: A preset stores project ids and plugin name, not a frozen copy of the systems.

requirements.statement: Saving a preset with fewer than two or more than six projects shows an error naming the 2–6 project limit and stores no preset, while two and six projects save successfully.
requirements.notes: The bundle selection limit inherited from R-202 also applies to a saved preset; boundary values 1, 2, 6 and 7.

requirements.source_phrase: Viewers can jump to lines, copy issues and see ignored items. Only Owners and Editors can fix, accept or ignore.
requirements.statement: A Viewer opening a project can click issues to jump, use Copy issues and open the Ignored (N) section, while Fix these, each row's Fix, Accept fix and Ignore are disabled or absent with a view-only explanation; an Owner or Editor sees those controls active.
requirements.notes: Build note says role controls are hidden/disabled in the screen; the server half is fix-role-be.

requirements.source_phrase: Viewers can jump to lines, copy issues and see ignored items. Only Owners and Editors can fix, accept or ignore.
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp and PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores from a Viewer are refused with no provider call and no stored ignore, while the same requests from an Editor or Owner of the project succeed; a Viewer's accepted fix cannot be saved because PUT /api/projects/{id} is refused.
requirements.notes: Both halves: refusal for the Viewer and success for the Editor, so over-refusal is detectable. The Save path is inherited R-073.

requirements.source_phrase: Fixes use the user's own AI key and current model, never the Universal Key.
requirements.statement: POST /api/ai/fix-cpp uses the provider and model the caller saved with the key (defaulting to Google Gemini gemini-3.5-flash-lite) and returns the model name it used, so the fix matches the model shown in the AI key window.
requirements.notes: The response carries model; the saved provider/model selection is inherited from R-146/R-158/R-159.

requirements.statement: The fix endpoint sends the caller's key only in the request header to the selected provider, stores the key in no project record, job document or response, and writes it into no log line including provider URLs logged on error.
requirements.notes: Secret-hygiene class applied to the new fix path; inherited R-167 and R-219 cover logs for generate and review, this covers fix-cpp.

requirements.statement: For a .h/.cpp pair with a missing own include and a class-name mismatch, POST /api/ai/fix-cpp returns a patch that resolves at least one of those named issues and leaves the header's unrelated declarations unchanged; a different pair with a different defect returns a different patch, so no fixed patch is reused.
requirements.notes: AI class: the output must answer the actual input and change when the input changes; seeded buggy pair from 'Health History Demo' has a known missing Engine/World.h.

requirements.statement: The fix review modal, the Ignored (N) section and the Bundle presets list render their primary content and Accept/Discard, Restore and preset open/rename/delete controls without overlap or clipping at 1440px and at 375px wide, with the side-by-side diff readable at both widths.
requirements.notes: Layout class on the new surfaces; the build's known gap says no phone layout is built, so Phase 4 should report it.

requirements.statement: The fix modal's running, diff, error and no-changes states look visibly different; Accept and Discard are disabled while running and after Accept succeeds, and closing the modal returns to the C++ tab with the previous compile-check results unchanged.
requirements.notes: UI-state class: loading, disabled, selected and error states must be distinguishable.

requirements.source_phrase: An owner creates a team (name plus members by email, each with Editor or Viewer).
requirements.statement: From the Projects panel's Team tab a signed-in user opens the team modal, enters a team name and adds at least one member by email with an Editor or Viewer role, and on save the team appears in the team switcher with the name exactly as typed and those members listed with their roles.
requirements.notes: Entry point of the team area; the modal fields named in the build description are team-name-input, team-invite-email/role/submit and team-save-button.

requirements.source_phrase: An owner creates a team (name plus members by email, each with Editor or Viewer).
requirements.statement: POST /api/teams creates a team owned by the caller with the posted name and members, and GET /api/teams returns exactly the teams the caller belongs to with their members and roles, so a user in two teams receives both and a non-member receives neither.
requirements.notes: Scoping is by membership, not by a client-supplied id.

requirements.source_phrase: they receive the email and join
requirements.statement: Inviting an address to a team records a pending invite shown in the team modal with its address and role, and the invited person who opens the emailed link and signs in with that address becomes a member with the assigned role and finds the team in the switcher.
requirements.notes: Build UI: team-invite-email/role/submit and the member rows.

requirements.source_phrase: team invites, project share invites and password-reset requests are sent as real emails from "UE5 System Architect"
requirements.statement: POST /api/teams/{id}/members records the invitation bound to that team and role, sends the invite email and returns an emailed flag reporting whether the provider accepted the message, and the invite stays pending and acceptable when delivery failed.
requirements.notes: Build notes say example.com addresses come back emailed=false and delivered@resend.dev true; Phase 4 should confirm the flag tracks the provider rather than a hard-coded domain check.

requirements.source_phrase: they receive the email and join
requirements.statement: Opening /team-invite/{token} while signed in with the invited address joins that team once and shows the team's projects, while opening it signed in with a different address shows a refusal naming the email mismatch and joins nothing.
requirements.notes: Build page: TeamInviteAccept in AuthPages.jsx.

requirements.source_phrase: they receive the email and join
requirements.statement: POST /api/team-invites/{token}/accept adds the caller to the invited team only when the caller's email equals the invited address, applies the invited role, is refused with no membership on a mismatched email or a second use, and grants no access to any other team.
requirements.notes: Single use, address-bound and tenant-bound in one promise.

requirements.source_phrase: Owners can rename the team, change roles, remove members or delete the team.
requirements.statement: The team modal lets the owner rename the team, change a member between Editor and Viewer, remove a member, and delete the team after a confirmation naming it, with each change reflected in place and still in effect after a page reload.
requirements.notes: Build UI: team-role-*, team-remove-*, team-delete-button.

requirements.source_phrase: Owners can rename the team, change roles, remove members or delete the team.
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/teams/{id} renames the team, PATCH /api/teams/{id}/members/{uid} changes that member's role, DELETE on the member removes them and DELETE /api/teams/{id} deletes the team, each allowed only to the team owner and refused with no stored change for any other member.
requirements.notes: Both halves needed: the owner's success and the non-owner's refusal.

requirements.source_phrase: Deleting a team moves its projects back to their creators.
requirements.statement: Deleting a team clears team_id on its projects and presets so each project returns to its creator's Mine list, is no longer returned to the other former members, and a direct GET by a former member is refused with no field of the project.
requirements.notes: Build note: deleting a team unsets team_id.

requirements.source_phrase: A project or bundle preset can be moved into a team, and then everyone in it has access with their team role.
requirements.statement: The move control on an owned project in the Projects panel assigns it to one of the caller's teams, after which the project shows a team badge in the list, appears under the Team tab for every member with their team role, and the assignment survives a reload.
requirements.notes: Build UI: project-move-{id} select on owned projects, project-team-badge-*.

requirements.source_phrase: Moving a project into a team requires being its owner.
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/team sets the project's team when the caller owns the project, is refused with 403 and no change when the caller does not own it (including a member holding the team's Editor role), and afterwards the project is returned to every member of that team with their team role.
requirements.notes: Build check: non-owner move returns 403.

requirements.source_phrase: move projects and presets in and out
requirements.statement: The project's owner can move it out of its team, after which team_id is cleared, the project returns to the creator's Mine list, and other team members' GET of it is refused and it appears in none of their lists.
requirements.notes: The plan says projects and presets move in and out; the out direction is the paranoid half of the move.

requirements.source_phrase: The Projects panel gets a third tab, "Team", with a team switcher if someone belongs to several.
requirements.statement: The Projects panel shows a third tab 'Team' listing the selected team's projects and presets with a small team badge, a switcher lists each team by name when the user belongs to more than one, and a user who belongs to no team sees an explicit empty message with a create-team action.
requirements.notes: Build UI: projects-tab-team, team-switcher.

requirements.source_phrase: Everyone sees them in the Team tab.
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects returns each project under exactly one of mine, shared or team for the caller, where team holds the projects of teams the caller belongs to and never a project of a team the caller is not in.
requirements.notes: Build: GET /api/projects returns mine/shared/team; mutual exclusion is the testable part.

requirements.source_phrase: A project or bundle preset can be moved into a team
requirements.statement: A Bundle preset row has a move control assigning it to one of the caller's teams, after which team members see it in their Bundle presets list with a team badge and the move survives a reload.
requirements.notes: Build UI: preset-move-* on preset rows.

requirements.source_phrase: A project or bundle preset can be moved into a team
requirements.statement: POST /api/bundle-presets/{id}/team sets the preset's team when the caller created it, is refused with no change when anyone else asks, and GET /api/bundle-presets afterwards returns the preset to a team member who can open every project in it.
requirements.notes: Creator-only move plus the visibility rule for team presets.

requirements.source_phrase: A team role and a direct project share don't add up: the higher of the two applies.
requirements.statement: The workspace a member reaches through both a team role and a direct share enables exactly the controls of the higher role, so save and fix controls are active for an Editor direct share over a Viewer team role and disabled for the reverse.
requirements.notes: UI half of the precedence rule; the server half is role-precedence-be.

requirements.source_phrase: A team role and a direct project share don't add up: the higher of the two applies.
requirements.statement: For a project both inside a team and shared directly with the same user the server applies the higher of the two roles, so a team Viewer with an Editor share can PATCH and save the project and a team Editor with a Viewer share can also save, while two Viewer roles refuse every write.
requirements.notes: Effective role is computed per request from both sources.

requirements.source_phrase: each with Editor or Viewer
requirements.statement: A team Viewer's PATCH of the project, PUT of its ignores, POST to /api/ai/fix-cpp and POST to /api/projects/{id}/team are each refused with 403 and no stored change, while the same four requests from the team's Editor succeed.
requirements.notes: Build check: team viewer cannot PATCH settings (403); the Editor half proves no over-refusal.

requirements.source_phrase: Per-project sharing still works for people outside the team.
requirements.statement: A project inside a team can still be shared directly with a person outside the team as Editor or Viewer, and that person finds it under Shared with me with the shared role while team members see it under Team.
requirements.notes: Over-refusal check: moving a project into a team must not block sharing outside it.

requirements.source_phrase: Per-project sharing still works for people outside the team.
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/members on a team project records a direct share for an address outside the team with its role, and GET /api/projects returns the project to that person under shared with that role and to team members under team.

requirements.source_phrase: set a new password from the link
requirements.statement: Opening the emailed reset link shows a form asking for the new password; submitting it saves the password once, shows a success message and lets the account sign in with the new password, while a used or expired link shows a refusal instead of the form.
requirements.notes: Build page: ForgotPassword in AuthPages.jsx with forgot-email-input, forgot-submit, forgot-sent.

requirements.source_phrase: The sender name is "UE5 System Architect".
requirements.statement: The reset email is sent server-side through Emergent's managed email service with the sender name 'UE5 System Architect', a subject naming the reset, one link that opens the app's reset page directly, and a footer stating the app never asks for passwords by email, with no email account or key required and no key reaching the browser.
requirements.notes: Third-party and messaging classes: managed email service, sender identity, link target and footer copy are all part of the promise.

requirements.source_phrase: Emails go only to addresses the inviting user typed or to the account requesting a reset. There are no bulk emails.
requirements.statement: The email service is called only with the single address the inviting user typed or the address of the account that requested the reset, and no request accepts a list of recipients or causes more than one message per invite or reset request.
requirements.notes: Prevents the app being used as a relay; required_credentials also says only delivered@resend.dev may receive real test mail.

requirements.source_phrase: On-screen links remain as a fallback when sending fails (shown only to the person who sent the invite).
requirements.statement: When a project share invite cannot be delivered the Share modal shows the copyable invite link to the sender only and marks the invite as not delivered, while a delivered invite shows the delivered state and no on-screen link is shown to the invited person.
requirements.notes: Replaces the earlier link-only delivery; the sender-only visibility is the privacy half.

requirements.source_phrase: team invites, project share invites and password-reset requests are sent as real emails from "UE5 System Architect"
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/members records the invite, sends the share email and returns an emailed flag reporting delivery, the invite stays acceptable when delivery failed, and the fallback link is present only in the response to the inviting user.
requirements.notes: Build: returns emailed true|false|null; undeliverable domains return false and delivered@resend.dev true.

requirements.statement: Each pending invite in the team modal and the Share modal shows a delivery state of delivered, failed or not attempted taken from the emailed flag rather than assumed, and the same state appears after a page reload.
requirements.notes: Build: the flag is true|false|null, which maps to delivered, failed and not attempted; build description says the on-screen link appears only for the sender when sending fails.

requirements.source_phrase: the Event Graph tab gets a "Copy for Unreal" button. It copies the graph in Unreal's own clipboard text format, so pasting into a Blueprint editor (Ctrl+V) creates the real nodes and wires.
requirements.statement: The Event Graph tab's 'Copy for Unreal' chip puts Unreal clipboard text for the displayed graph on the clipboard, shows a toast of the form 'Copied N of M nodes' and a hint naming the Blueprint Event Graph to paste into, and pasting into a text editor shows node and wire entries rather than a JSON dump.
requirements.notes: Build: copyForUnreal in Workspace.jsx with toast 'Copied N of M nodes'; judged by pasting the clipboard, not by the toast alone.

requirements.source_phrase: It covers common node types: events, function calls on the generated component, branches, variables (get/set), sequence and delays.
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects/{id} returns each event-graph node with a type from events, function calls on the generated component, branches, variable get, variable set, sequence and delay, and each edge with the pins it connects, so the client can render Unreal clipboard text for every node of the stored graph.
requirements.notes: The clipboard text is built client-side from the stored graph; the backend promise is that node types and pins survive a new session.

requirements.source_phrase: Anything it can't map becomes a clearly labeled comment node instead of being dropped.
requirements.statement: A node of a type the clipboard mapper does not support appears in the copied text as a comment node labelled with the node's title and type, so the pasted node count equals the graph's node count and no node is dropped.
requirements.notes: Count in the toast is the check: N equals M only if nothing was dropped.

requirements.statement: Copy for Unreal on a graph with no nodes copies nothing meaningful and shows a message saying the graph is empty, without throwing or leaving the previous clipboard content in place.
requirements.notes: Empty state of the new control; a stale clipboard would paste a previous graph into Unreal.

requirements.source_phrase: Plugin zips also include the paste text as a file per graph.
requirements.statement: A plugin zip contains Blueprints/<GraphName>_EventGraph.txt for each graph of the project, and each file's text equals what the Copy for Unreal button produces for that graph.
requirements.notes: Build file: zipExport.js writes Blueprints/*_EventGraph.txt alongside the module.

requirements.source_phrase: Tests are generated on request with the user's own AI key (1 request), shown in a new **Tests** tab, run through the compile check like the main code, and can be fixed the same way.
requirements.statement: A Tests tab beside C++ has a Generate tests button; pressing it shows a running state and then the generated spec tests in a code viewer with line numbers, a compile-check summary for the test file, and per-issue Fix access through the same before/after review as the main code.
requirements.notes: Build UI: tab-tests, generate-tests-button, tests-cases, tests-check-summary, codebox-tests-code.

requirements.source_phrase: Tests are generated on request with the user's own AI key (1 request)
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/tests makes exactly one provider request with the caller's own key, stores the returned test source with the project, returns it, and returns 400 naming the missing user key and stores nothing when no key is sent.
requirements.notes: Build: server.py generate_tests; key comes per request, never stored.

requirements.source_phrase: each system can produce Unreal automation tests (C++ "spec" tests) that check its core behavior, such as "damage lowers health", "health never goes below 0" and "regen stops at max".
requirements.statement: The generated test file is C++ automation spec source naming the system's own parameters and behaviours — for a health system a test asserting damage lowers health and one asserting health never drops below zero — differs between two different systems, and an empty or non-C++ reply fails the request instead of being stored.
requirements.notes: AI class: judged on the content of the test source for a system whose right answer is known in advance.

requirements.source_phrase: A test file is kept with the project and marked "out of date" when the system changes.
requirements.statement: After the system's C++ changes, the Tests tab shows the stored tests with an 'out of date' marker and a regenerate action; regenerating replaces the stored tests and clears the marker, and a page reload shows the tests with the current marker state.
requirements.notes: Build UI: tests-stale appears when C++ changes.

requirements.source_phrase: A test file is kept with the project and marked "out of date" when the system changes.
requirements.statement: The project stores its generated tests and a tests_stale flag; a synthesis, a save whose C++ differs or an accepted fix sets tests_stale true, a successful test generation sets it false and replaces the stored test source, and GET /api/projects/{id} returns both.
requirements.notes: Persistence half of the out-of-date marker.

requirements.source_phrase: Test generation uses the user's own AI key and counts toward the daily usage counter, the same as fixes.
requirements.statement: Each test-generation request that reaches the provider increments the caller's daily usage count by one, and GET /api/ai/usage reflects the new count for that user only.
requirements.notes: Extends inherited R-174/R-175 to the tests path.

requirements.source_phrase: Tests are not generated automatically with every synthesis.
requirements.statement: POST /api/generate starts no test generation and stores no test source, so a freshly synthesized project's Tests tab offers generation rather than showing tests.
requirements.notes: A promise of absence; a synthesis that quietly spends a second AI request is the failure.

requirements.source_phrase: Plugin exports place them in the plugin as a test-only module that runs from Unreal's Session Frontend > Automation panel.
requirements.statement: A plugin zip for a project with tests contains Source/<Name>Tests/ with a Build.cs, the module entry file and the generated spec test source, and the .uplugin lists that module so Unreal's Session Frontend > Automation panel can run the tests.
requirements.notes: Build file: zipExport.js writeModule for the tests module.

requirements.statement: The Tests tab's empty, generating, generated, stale and error states look visibly different, Generate tests is disabled while a generation runs, and a failed generation shows an error where the tests would be rather than an empty code viewer.
requirements.notes: UI-state class applied to the new tab.

requirements.source_phrase: the system's tunable values (damage, regen rate, max health, cooldowns) export as a CSV Data Table plus a matching row struct in the C++.
requirements.statement: A plugin zip contains Data/<Class>_Tuning.csv whose header names each tunable parameter and whose single data row holds its values, plus <Class>TuningRow.h and .cpp declaring a row struct whose fields correspond to the CSV columns.
requirements.notes: Build file: unrealExtras.js; judged by opening the CSV and the struct, not by the export status.

requirements.source_phrase: The generated code reads its defaults from that table when one is assigned, so designers can tweak numbers in Unreal without recompiling.
requirements.statement: The exported C++ reads each tunable parameter's default from the assigned Data Table row when one is set and keeps the built-in default when none is assigned, with the same parameter names in the code, the row struct and the CSV.
requirements.notes: One parameter name in three places; the build assumption keeps built-in defaults when no table is assigned.

requirements.source_phrase: The Setup guide gains steps for importing the table and assigning it.
requirements.statement: The Setup Guide for a system with tunable values includes numbered steps for importing the Data Table CSV and assigning the table to the generated component, each step carrying its Why note.
requirements.notes: The guide is stored with the project and rendered in the Setup Guide tab.

requirements.source_phrase: every zip (single plugin, source-only and bundle) includes `COMPILE_REPORT.md`.
requirements.statement: Every downloaded zip — single plugin, source-only and bundle — contains COMPILE_REPORT.md at its root and the source-only download contains it too, opening as readable Markdown rather than an empty or truncated file.
requirements.notes: Build checks: plugin zip and source-only zip both carry COMPILE_REPORT.md.

requirements.source_phrase: It lists the date, the model used for any AI review, every current issue (errors and warnings), every ignored issue with who ignored it, and fixes applied since the last save.
requirements.statement: COMPILE_REPORT.md lists the export date, the model used for any AI review, every current non-ignored issue with file and line, every ignored issue with the name of the user who ignored it, and each fix applied since the last save, and a project with no issues writes a report stating none were found.
requirements.notes: Judged by the file's content; the report is not an Unreal build and must not claim to be one.

requirements.source_phrase: Bundles get one section per module.
requirements.statement: A bundle's COMPILE_REPORT.md has one section per bundled module, each listing that module's issues, ignores and fixes, so a bundle of two projects produces two sections and no module's issues appear under another's.
requirements.notes: Guards against one module's issues being attributed to the wrong module.

requirements.statement: PUT /api/projects/{id}/ignores records for each ignored issue key the user who ignored it and the issue's line text, and GET /api/projects/{id} returns them, so the export can name who ignored an issue and drop the ignore when that line's text changes.
requirements.notes: Build description: the compile report names who ignored each issue, which inherited R-240 does not store; this extends it.

requirements.source_phrase: Add a "Fix and regenerate" option for structural problems
requirements.statement: The compile-check header has a 'Fix and regenerate' action that regenerates the whole system with the current issues as change requests, shows a running state, and on completion opens the Compare tab diffing the new system against the previous one, and the same action is offered when a patch cannot be applied.
requirements.notes: Build: new button in the compile check, also offered from the patch-failed error; 1 synthesis.

requirements.source_phrase: Add a "Fix and regenerate" option for structural problems
requirements.statement: POST /api/generate with the project's current issues as change requests starts one synthesis with the caller's key, stores the result as a new version whose note names the compile issues addressed, leaves the previous system and every earlier version intact, and increments the daily usage count once.
requirements.notes: Build: note reads 'Regenerated to fix 1 compile issue'; the previous version must remain restorable.

requirements.statement: For a project whose compile check reports a missing own include, the regenerated system's code includes that header and keeps the project's other modules and parameters, while a different issue set produces a different regenerated system.
requirements.notes: AI class: content right for its input and changing with the input; 'Health History Demo' has a known missing Engine/World.h.

requirements.source_phrase: Auto-fill fix history notes with accepted changes
requirements.statement: After an accepted fix, pressing Save opens the note field pre-filled with a one-line note naming the change, the text is editable before saving, the stored version shows the edited text, and undoing the fix removes its note from the next save's pre-fill.
requirements.notes: Build: note read 'Fixed: Add #include Engine/World.h for GetWorld()'; Undo fix also removes its note.

requirements.source_phrase: Pre-fill the save note, editable
requirements.statement: The version snapshot created after an accepted fix records the note the user submits, which is the pre-filled fix note unless edited; a save after Fix and regenerate records a note naming the compile issues; after an Undo fix the pre-filled note names the undone fix instead of the original one.
requirements.notes: The stored note must be the user's final text, not the pre-filled default.

requirements.source_phrase: Per project, saved for the whole team
requirements.statement: The UE5 .zip menu has an auto-fix-before-export checkbox whose state is stored on the project for the whole team, an Owner or Editor can change it, a Viewer sees it read-only, and the state is the same after a reload and for a teammate who reopens the project.
requirements.notes: Answer to the ask_human question about where the setting lives; build note: only Owners and Editors can change it.

requirements.source_phrase: Per project, saved for the whole team
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/projects/{id} stores auto_fix_before_export on the project and GET /api/projects/{id} returns it to every member, while a Viewer's PATCH of that field is refused with 403 and no stored change and an Editor's succeeds.
requirements.notes: Both halves: the Editor's write and the Viewer's refusal.

requirements.source_phrase: Show the before/after review first
requirements.statement: With auto-fix on and current issues present, choosing an export opens the before/after review first with 'Accept fix and export' and 'Discard and export'; accepting downloads the zip built from the patched code, discarding downloads the zip built from the unpatched code, and no zip downloads before one of them is pressed.
requirements.notes: Answer to the ask_human question about what happens to the auto-fix's changes: the review is shown first.

requirements.source_phrase: Show the before/after review first
requirements.statement: When the project's auto-fix flag is on and the compile check reports issues, the export path calls POST /api/ai/fix-cpp with the issues and both files before any zip is assembled, returns the patch and change list for review, assembles no zip until an accept or discard decision, and on a fix failure offers an export without fixing that proceeds with the unpatched code.
requirements.notes: Build: buttons become 'Accept fix and export' / 'Discard and export'; a failed fix offers 'Export without fixing'.

requirements.statement: With auto-fix on but no saved AI key, or for a Viewer, choosing an export opens the normal export-check warning with 'Export anyway' instead of a fix review and sends no fix request.
requirements.notes: Build description: with no AI key or for Viewers the export falls back to the normal warning.

requirements.statement: On a project with unsaved changes the auto-fix checkbox shows 'Save the project to turn this on' and does not enable, while a saved project enables it.
requirements.notes: Build description: the setting only works on saved projects.

requirements.statement: The auto-fix checkbox, the fix review's running state, the 'Accept fix and export' and 'Discard and export' buttons and the 'Export without fixing' fallback are visibly distinct from one another, and nothing downloads while the fix is running.
requirements.notes: UI-state class on the new export path.

requirements.source_phrase: Anyone who can open all its projects
requirements.statement: A preset created by a teammate appears in the Bundle presets list marked 'from <name>' when the signed-in user can open every project in it and is absent from the list when they cannot open one of them, and only its creator sees the rename and delete controls.
requirements.notes: Build: the shared row is marked 'from <name>'; only the creator can rename or delete it.

requirements.source_phrase: Enable sharing of bundle presets among teammates
requirements.statement: GET /api/bundle-presets returns the caller's own presets plus presets shared with them for which the caller can open every project, each carrying its creator's name, omits a preset with at least one project the caller cannot open, and returns 403 with no stored change for a PATCH or DELETE from anyone but the creator.
requirements.notes: Visibility follows project access; mutability follows creation.

requirements.statement: Opening a shared preset fills the bundle dialog with its plugin name and its readable projects ticked from their latest saved versions, and lists any project the user can no longer open as skipped without failing the open.
requirements.notes: Build description: opening a preset uses the latest saved versions and lists skipped projects.

requirements.source_phrase: Batch Fix Projects: Run Fix these across every project in a bundle preset before downloading the plugin
requirements.statement: The bundle window has a 'Fix all projects' action that runs Fix these on each selected project with issues, showing one review at a time labelled with the project's position ('Project N of M') and a Skip control that moves on without changing that project, and the download then uses each project's resulting code.
requirements.notes: Answer to the ask_human question: one review per project, one after another.

requirements.source_phrase: Save each accepted fix as a new version
requirements.statement: For each project in the batch the caller can edit, accepting its fix saves the patched code as a new version with a fix note; for a project the caller can only view, the accepted patch is used in that download only and no version is written; a skipped project's stored system is unchanged.
requirements.notes: Answer to the ask_human question about what happens to the projects after a batch fix.

requirements.statement: Each project's fix in a batch makes one provider request and increments the caller's daily usage count once per request, and the batch warns and asks for confirmation when the selected model is near its free limit before the first request is sent.
requirements.notes: Build description: 1 request per project with the same near-limit warning as synthesis; mirrors inherited R-183 and R-238.

requirements.source_phrase: Clean Export Badge: Show a "compile-checked" badge in the plugin README when an export passed with no issues
requirements.statement: A plugin README from an export whose compile check found no errors starts with a green 'compile-checked: no errors' badge and the export date, warnings do not withhold the badge and are listed beneath it, and any remaining error or AI-review finding omits the badge.
requirements.notes: Answer to the ask_human question: badge when there are no errors, warnings allowed; build adds that ignored issues do not count and AI findings do.

requirements.source_phrase: No errors, warnings allowed
requirements.statement: For a bundle, the README's module table has a 'Compile check' column showing each module's result, and the top badge appears only when every module has no errors.
requirements.notes: Build description: bundles get a per-module compile-check column and an all-modules badge rule.

requirements.source_phrase: No errors, warnings allowed
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects/{id} returns the current ignored issue keys with their line text and the last AI review's findings for the project, so the export's badge and issue list are computed from the same state the C++ tab shows, an ignored error never withholds the badge and an AI-review finding does.
requirements.notes: The badge is a judgment on the state the screen shows; the backend must expose that same state at download time.

requirements.source_phrase: Fix History Panel: Show every accepted fix per version in History, with a one-click way to see its before/after again
requirements.statement: The History window shows under each version an 'N fix' chip listing the fixes accepted before that save and, separately, the fixes not yet saved, and clicking a fix reopens its before/after diff with removed lines in red and added lines in green.
requirements.notes: Build: History lists a 'N fix' chip per version plus unsaved fixes.

requirements.source_phrase: Fix History Panel: Show every accepted fix per version in History, with a one-click way to see its before/after again
requirements.statement: Each saved version stores the fixes applied before that save — file, before text and after text per fix — GET /api/projects/{id}/versions returns them with the version, and unsaved fixes are returned separately so the History window can show both.
requirements.notes: Build: each accepted fix is saved with the next version; unsaved fixes are listed too.

requirements.source_phrase: View it and undo just that fix
requirements.statement: A past fix's before/after view has an 'Undo this fix' action that puts that fix's before lines back into the workspace as an unsaved edit, pre-fills the next save note with 'Undid fix: …' and leaves the other accepted fixes in place, and when the nearby code has changed since it shows an error and changes nothing.
requirements.notes: Answer to the ask_human question: view a past fix and undo just that fix.

requirements.source_phrase: View it and undo just that fix
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/fixes/{fix_id}/undo returns the restored code and writes no version when the target lines still match after surrounding shifts, returns an error with no change when they cannot be reapplied, and leaves the stored version history unchanged until the user saves.
requirements.notes: Undo is a workspace edit, not a version; the shifted-lines case is the failure path.

requirements.statement: After the owner removes a member from the team, that member's next GET /api/projects returns none of the team's projects and a direct GET of one is refused with no field of it, within one request of the removal.
requirements.notes: Tier-1 second-actor half of team membership: removal must take effect on the next request, not at the next sign-in.

requirements.statement: Changing a member's team role from Editor to Viewer takes effect on that member's next request, so their PATCH of a team project is refused while their GET still returns the project read-only.
requirements.notes: Same next-request rule as inherited R-114, extended to team roles.

requirements.source_phrase: A person can belong to several teams. Each team has one owner.
requirements.statement: A user can create and belong to several teams, and each team's member list holds exactly one member with the owner role — its creator — so no second owner can be stored for the same team.
requirements.notes: Identity rule for the team: membership is per team, ownership is singular.

requirements.source_phrase: Existing on-screen invite and reset links keep working until they expire.
requirements.statement: An on-screen invite link or reset link issued before the email flow still opens its accept or reset page and works once until its expiry, and an expired one shows a refusal rather than the form.
requirements.notes: Backwards compatibility promise made by the plan; a link that stops working after the email release is a finding.

requirements.statement: Opening /team-invite/{token} while signed out redirects to sign-in and returns to the accept page afterwards, joining the team only after signing in with the invited address.
requirements.notes: Auth class: the emailed link lands on a protected page before the recipient has a session.

requirements.source_phrase: The zip contains the code, tests module, Data Table CSV, Blueprint paste files and `COMPILE_REPORT.md`.
requirements.statement: A plugin zip for a system with tests and tunable values contains the module source, the Source/<Name>Tests module, Data/<Class>_Tuning.csv, Blueprints/<Graph>_EventGraph.txt and COMPILE_REPORT.md, and a source-only zip contains the code files and COMPILE_REPORT.md, each file non-empty and named for the class, module or graph it holds.
requirements.notes: Files class: judged by opening the archive and reading each file, not by the download response.

requirements.statement: Each file in an export equals the stored value it is named after — the .h and .cpp equal the stored code, the CSV values equal the stored tunables, the clipboard text equals the stored graph and the report's issues equal the current check — so no export carries another project's or another version's content.
requirements.notes: Catches an export built from a stale or wrong project; the agent's own note about a long-open bundle window is the risk this covers.

requirements.statement: Downloading a bundle re-reads each selected project's current saved system at download time, so a project a teammate saved after the bundle window was opened is exported at its latest version once the window is reopened, and no export uses a stale copy of a project.
requirements.notes: Inherited R-253 says presets use latest saved versions; the agent's known gap (long-open bundle window exports what was saved when opened) is the gap this requirement records.

requirements.statement: The /forgot page shows the same sent confirmation for an unknown address as for a known one, so the screen never reveals whether an account exists.
requirements.notes: Auth class enumeration half of the generic forgot-password reply.

requirements.statement: After a successful reset the sign-in screen accepts the new password and refuses the old one, and reloading the used reset URL shows the refusal instead of the form.

requirements.statement: The Tests tab, the Team tab and team modal, the /forgot page, the fix review and the bundle window with 'Fix all projects' render their primary controls without overlap or clipping at 1440px and at 375px wide, with the code viewer's line numbers visible at both widths.

requirements.statement: The team modal's create, invite, error and saved states look visibly different, its save button is disabled while a request is in flight, and a refused invite or an address already on the team shows a message in the user's terms.
requirements.notes: UI-state class; also the refusal half of a repeated invite.

requirements.statement: The Tests tab, the Team tab, /forgot and the bundle window load in the deployed app with no console error, missing module or undefined name, and each is reachable from the navigation a signed-in user sees.
requirements.notes: Build and deployment class applied to the release's new screens.

requirements.statement: The invite email names who invited the recipient, names the team or project they are invited to, and its single button lands on the accept page after sign-in, so a recipient who is not signed in is not stranded.
requirements.notes: benchmark: collaboration tools send invites that name the inviter and the destination and land on a page that works before sign-in.

requirements.statement: The reset form asks for the new password twice, refuses a mismatch and a password shorter than the product's minimum with a message naming the rule, and never renders the password in the page source.
requirements.notes: benchmark: every password-reset screen confirms the new password and enforces a minimum length before submitting.

requirements.statement: The Tests tab lists each generated test by its readable spec name with the assertion it makes, so a developer can tell what will run in the Automation panel without reading the whole file.
requirements.notes: benchmark: test surfaces list tests by name and outcome, not as one opaque code block.

requirements.statement: The Team tab shows each member's name, email and role, marks the owner, and lists pending invites separately from members, so an owner can see who has access before changing a role.
requirements.notes: benchmark: team management screens separate members from pending invites and mark the owner.
